title: King's Indian Defense: the ideas
line: Black lets White build a big center, then strikes at it.

steps.text: White starts by pushing the pawn in front of its queen two squares, into the center.
Bring the knight out. For now it stops White's other center pawn from coming to e4.

also.d7d5: That leads to the Queen's Gambit, also sound. This lesson goes on with the knight.

steps.text: Push the pawn on g7 one square, to make room for your bishop.

also.e7e6: That leads to the Nimzo-Indian or the Queen's Indian, also sound. This lesson goes on with the other pawn.

steps.text: Put the bishop in the gap. Once the knight moves, it aims at the center.

also.d7d5: That is the Grünfeld Defense, also sound. This lesson goes on with the bishop.

steps.after: White takes the whole center. Black lets it happen.

steps.text: Move the pawn in front of your queen one square. It guards e5, so White's pawn on e4 cannot safely push there.
steps.after: This is the King's Indian Defense.

steps.text: Castle: move your king two squares toward the rook. It is safe behind the bishop.
Why castle first: here Black struck before castling. White trades pawns and queens, the king takes back, and the pawn on e5 falls.
Now strike at the center: push the pawn in front of your king two squares.
steps.after: Your pawn attacks White's center, and White must decide what to do about it.

summary: Black lets White take the center, castles behind the bishop, then strikes at the center with a pawn.
